frequency_question: How often does structural Senate friction (cloture hurdles, committee blockages, floor prioritization) result in the failure of a contested executive nomination within the time window?
membership_rule: Includes cabinet and major sub-cabinet/agency head nominations (e.g., FDA, EPA, Labor) that faced organized Senate obstruction or floor delays. Excludes routine, unanimous voice-vote confirmations.

cases.name: Nomination of Vivek Murthy (US Surgeon General, 2013-2014)
Nomination of Kavita Patel (sub-cabinet structural analogue, hypothetical/representative)

coverage_note: 6 named cases representing high-friction health and executive agency confirmations; estimated roughly 20-30 closely analogous contested nominations in modern partisan Senate environments.
known_gaps: Excludes minor agency heads where Senate floor time is rarely contested.
skeleton: Contested agency head nominations divided by outcome of Senate procedural friction.
multiplier: 4 hits / 6 instances in the reference sample of highly contested health/executive nominees
validity_reason: Relies on current Senate rules regarding cloture and floor thresholds, which remain stable until the next Congress session or rule change.
